_doc: The run: the places in order, and which edge of each leads where (issue #4, D-020). A 'leg' is one visit to a place: the same place is a different leg on the way home, in another season, and it remembers what the men did there. 'exits' maps an edge of the place's map (its 'gates') to the next leg and the edge the men walk in by; an edge with no exit is closed. 'camera_elev' is how steeply the camera looks down on the ground, in degrees (D-051; the engine's own is 30). 'hours' is how long the walk between the two places takes on the clock. The whole world is grey-boxed (docs/world.md, #48, D-077): seven places on one trail, thirteen legs, out to the high ridge and home the same way.

night._doc: The night's hours on the clock run faster (speed, in hundredths of the day's), so a night by the fire is about a minute (#13).

season._doc: The season clock (#10, D-062). The year in thousandths of a season: 0 high summer, 1000 full autumn, 2000 midwinter, 3000 spring. 'start' is the year when the men leave; the clock moves one thousandth every 'ticks_per_milli' sim ticks while they are in a place, between that leg's 'year' ends. A leg's 'altitude' is how far its high ground runs ahead of the valley in autumn (and behind in spring). A leg with a 'season' instead stands still in it (the looks).

weather._doc: The weather (#15, D-063). It comes in spells of 'spell_hours' hours on the clock; 'chances' is how many spells in a hundred are mist, rain or snow in each season (the rest are clear). Rain falls as snow where snow lies. 'snow_slow' is how much of their pace lying snow takes off the men, in hundredths, and 'snowfall_slow' how much more snow coming down hard takes. A leg can name its own: "weather": "rain".

cover._doc: Cover (#9, D-064): how well a man is hidden on a tile, 0 to 100. Each old tree beside him gives 'tree_near' and each one two tiles off 'tree_far', times the leaves it still wears (a fir or pine all year; 'tall' is the deep wood's giants, whose crowns are far overhead), up to 'canopy_most' in all. A young tree beside him gives 'young', bracken on his tile 'bracken' (half in winter). A watcher's range is cut by up to 'hides' hundredths at full cover, and by 'night', 'mist', 'rain' and 'snow' hundredths at night and in that weather at its hardest.

ford._doc: Wading a ford (#20, D-065): a man's pace in the water in hundredths of his pace on dry ground, walking light ('wade') or with a load on his back ('loaded'), and how much more high water takes off ('high_water': at the height of the thaw, or in the hardest rain).

budget._doc: How big one place may be, so it loads behind the letter home and stays light to draw: tiles across and down, and how many old trees.

village_out._doc: Leg 1: leaving, at dawn in late summer. The men start at the top of the lane, by the west gate, with the village behind them.
village_out.name: The village edge

gorge_out._doc: The trail's bridge is found broken (#20, D-049): mend it with carried wood, or go down to the ford. The east gate leads on to the Roman ruins (#53, D-077; it led to the season's work, D-050).
gorge_out.name: The gorge

ridge._doc: Leg 7: the furthest point, in the first snow, and the turn for home (#55, D-077): the ridge has one gate, and the men go out by the way they came in.
ridge.name: The high ridge

pass_home._doc: Leg 8: the set piece (phase 2): the patrol follows the men, on the valley path far below the shelf (D-076), then up the ramp near the east gate and along the trail behind them (D-077, docs/threats.md). 'patrol': its road in tiles, how many, and how long after the men come in it sets out.
pass_home.name: The pass, going home

fir_woods_home.name: The deep fir woods, going home

village_home._doc: Leg 13: coming home in spring. The run ends when the men walk down the lane by the west gate (the homecoming and the ending come later, #51).
village_home.name: The village edge, coming home

camp_look._doc: Not on the route: the mock-up's beech clearing (archive picture 23), to compare the game beside it. leg:camp_look camp:29,31
camp_look.name: The beech clearing after leaf-fall

gorge_look._doc: Not on the route: the gorge with its bridge broken, to look at (#20). leg:gorge_look
gorge_look.name: The gorge

ruins_look._doc: Not on the route: the Roman ruins' props in a small beech clearing, to look at closely (#17). leg:ruins_look
ruins_look.name: The Roman road

letters._doc: PLACEHOLDERS written by Claude so the screen has words on it. The real letters are Dominic's to write or approve.
the_lane: I looked back from the top of the lane and you were still at the gate.
The fields are cut and the first oaks are behind us.
first_night: We came down through the beech valley today. The stream was low and easy to cross.
The trees here are older than the village. We look very small under them.
Tomorrow the fir woods. I think of you at every fire.
into_the_gorge: The trail on the mountain was buried under a fall of rock. We got by it.
They say the river in the gorge is high, and the bridge is old.
I keep your letter dry inside my coat.
the_old_road: We are over the river. Above it the old road runs, paved before our grandfathers' grandfathers.
The stones are cut so well that the water still runs off them.
I want to see how they did it.
up_to_the_pass: We climbed all day. The beeches gave way to pines, and the pines are thinning.
The pass is ahead, and the wind comes down it cold.
Keep the lamp in the window.
the_ridge: We came through the pass under a grey sky. It smells of snow up here.
Tomorrow the ridge, as far as we go.
From there every step is toward you.
turning_home: We stood on the ridge in the first snow and looked down on the far valley and its road.
There were riders on it. We turned for home.
Pray for an easy road back.
shelter_in_the_stones: We came down through the pass with the riders below us the whole way.
Tonight we sleep among the old stones, out of the wind.
down_to_the_river: Snow lies on the old road now. We went down to the river in it.
The gorge is next, and the bridge.
I count the places left between us.
through_the_snow: We came back over the river in the snow.
The firs are next, and they will be white and silent.
Every step now is a step toward you.
last_of_the_snow: We came down out of the firs today. The fall of rock is still there on the mountain.
Lower down the snow is going, and I heard water under it.
The beeches next, and then our own valley.
almost_home: The beeches are in leaf again. We passed the stumps of the trees we cut on the way out.
One more walk and I will see our roof.
